newsitem.title: UK: Suspected bomb found near N. Ireland base.
newsitem.headline: Suspected bomb found near N. Ireland base.

text.p: A suspected IRA bomb was found near a police base in the heart of Irish nationalist west Belfast on Thursday but a second guerrilla alert in the city seemed to have been a hoax, British security sources said.

The incidents come at a time of tension in Northern Ireland. IRA guerrillas have refused Anglo-Irish demands that they abandon a 28-year-old war to get their Sinn Fein political wing into peace talks.

A device was discovered in the Falls Roads area after the guerrilla Irish Republican Army telephoned media organisations saying a mortar bomb intended to hit police and army patrols had failed to detonate.
Streets around the heavily defended Andersonstown police station were cordoned off while army bomb disposal experts moved in.
"They have found something which is now being looked at," a police source.
Ian Williamson, police commander in west Belfast, condemned the guerrillas for what he termed their "grubby, pathetic but lethal little war".

Police and soldiers also launched a separate operation in the Antrim Road area of north Belfast after an IRA message to local media that their "volunteers" had been forced to abandon a powerful mortar bomb in a car after spotting police patrols. Later police said they had checked a suspect car but there was no bomb in it.
The IRA is fighting to end Britain's rule over Northern Ireland and unite the province with the Irish Republic.
Joe Hendron, a nationalist legislator with the Catholic Social Democratic and Labour Party, condemned the incidents and urged the IRA to call off a war that has intensified over recent months.
"The people are so very very tired of all this and they do want the republican leadership to call all this off and genuinely to go down the road of peace," he told BBC radio.
Police said they were investigating an attack by men who said they were from the IRA on a 16-year-old girl in Armagh city west of Belfast.

They said two men claiming to be from the organisation took her from a taxi office before midnight on Wednesday to a housing estate where they tied her to a lamp post. "She was slapped about the face by her attackers. Her hair was cut and paint was poured over her."
